And now let us go have a drink together.
Although no, you have to go to work early tomorrow.
Then I will drink, and you will sit for company.
Changes in life come like old age and like time.
Sometimes we run from them, thinking that everything can be left as it is.
Lena, forgive me for yesterday, it turned out awkwardly.
You understand too, I am the way I am, it is too late to change.
Either accept me or do not accept me, it is up to you to decide.
But changes in our life happen anyway, whether we want that or not.

No, we can accept them or try to stay in the past.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Ну вот, и завтра ты тоже барменом будешь.
examples.trans: Well there, and tomorrow you will be a bartender too.

examples.text: А я тогда завтра известным юристом стану!
examples.trans: And then tomorrow I will become a famous lawyer!

examples.text: Завтра утром снова выходи на работу.
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning report to work again.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нова').

meanings.en: to go out, to come out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'come out / report', paired with 'выйти'.

examples.text: Завтра утром снова выходи на работу.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.en: to drink up, to have a drink

examples.text: Можно я выпью капельку пива?

meanings.en: to turn out, to work out
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'turned out', paired with 'получаться'.

examples.text: Всё получится!
examples.trans: It will all work out!

examples.text: Из него получится хороший врач.
examples.trans: He'll make a good doctor.

examples.text: Классный из тебя мэр получится, Самсон.
examples.trans: You'll make a great mayor, Samson.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'also', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я тоже не понимаю, встречаемся мы или нет.
examples.trans: I also do not understand whether we are dating or not.

examples.text: Тоже мне великий актёр нашёлся!
examples.trans: Some great actor he turns out to be!

examples.text: Вчера был барменом, и сегодня тоже бармен.
examples.trans: Yesterday I was a bartender, and today I am a bartender too.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.text: Всё с тобой понятно, значит, в гости пришла.
examples.trans: Everything is clear with you, so you came for a visit.

examples.text: Я не понял, а кто давал команду пить?
examples.trans: I do not understand, who gave the order to drink?

examples.text: Я хотел быть похожим на вас, а сейчас понял, что лучше Воронеж, чем с вами на одной кухне!
examples.trans: I wanted to be like you, and now I understood that Voronezh is better than being in the same kitchen with you!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'such, what sort', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Хорошо, милая, как скажешь, так и будет.
examples.trans: Alright, darling, as you say, so it will be.

examples.text: Вы на свадьбу так красиво оделись?
examples.trans: Did you dress up so nicely for a wedding?

examples.text: Сегодня наш любимый клуб «Спартак» играет.
examples.trans: Today our favorite club Spartak is playing.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'здно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Поздравляю, только не забудь купить нам хороший сок.
examples.trans: Congratulations, just do not forget to buy us some good juice.

examples.text: Ты тоже пойми, я такой, как есть, поздно меняться.
examples.trans: You understand too, I am the way I am, it is too late to change.

examples.text: Беги, Марина, пока не поздно!
examples.trans: Run, Marina, before it's too late!

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to change', paired with 'поменяться'.

examples.text: Ты тоже пойми, я такой, как есть, поздно меняться.
examples.trans: You understand too, I am the way I am, it is too late to change.

examples.text: Люди меняются к лучшему.
examples.trans: People change for the better.

examples.text: Всё вокруг меняется.
examples.trans: Everything around is changing.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'or', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я тоже не понимаю, встречаемся мы или нет.
examples.trans: I also do not understand whether we are dating or not.

examples.text: Мы же с тобой в кино ходили три раза.
examples.trans: After all, you and I went to the movies three times.

examples.text: Всё, договорились, твоё условие принято.
examples.trans: That is it, we agreed, your condition is accepted.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нимать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'accept', paired with 'принять'.

examples.text: Ты или принимай меня, или не принимай, тебе решать.
examples.trans: Either accept me or do not accept me, it is up to you to decide.

examples.text: Мэр сегодня не принимает.
examples.trans: The mayor isn't seeing anyone today.

examples.text: Врач принимает утром.
examples.trans: The doctor sees patients in the morning.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если, конечно, футбол тебе дороже, чем я.
examples.trans: If, of course, football is dearer to you than I am.

examples.text: Сказал, что его блюда едят только в ресторане.
examples.trans: He said that his dishes are eaten only in the restaurant.

examples.text: Вот как с ним бороться, я не понимаю.
examples.trans: How to deal with him, I do not understand.

meanings.en: to decide, to make up one's mind
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to decide, to solve', paired with 'решить'.

examples.text: Дима, ты хозяин, ты здесь решаешь.
examples.trans: Dima, you are the owner, you decide here.

examples.text: А кем ты будешь работать на моей кухне, это мне решать.
examples.trans: And what you will work as in my kitchen is up to me to decide.

examples.text: Лена, ты что делаешь, это же решающий пенальти!
examples.trans: Lena, what are you doing, this is a decisive penalty kick!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если, конечно, футбол тебе дороже, чем я.
examples.trans: If, of course, football is dearer to you than I am.

examples.text: Мы же с тобой в кино ходили три раза.
examples.trans: After all, you and I went to the movies three times.

examples.text: Вчера, когда ты в кино крепко уснула.
examples.trans: Yesterday, when you fell fast asleep at the movies.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Наш шеф уволил курьера по доставке еды.
examples.trans: Our chef fired the food delivery courier.

examples.text: Меня наш шеф обратно не возьмёт.
examples.trans: Our chef will not take me back.

examples.text: Сегодня наш любимый клуб «Спартак» играет.
examples.trans: Today our favorite club Spartak is playing.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: В смысле, у меня сегодня правда выходной?
examples.trans: Wait, do I really have a day off today?

examples.text: Здравствуйте, уважаемый Дмитрий Владимирович.
examples.trans: Hello, respected Dmitry Vladimirovich.

examples.text: Это прекрасно, правда?
examples.trans: That is wonderful, isn't it?

meanings.en: to happen, take place, go on
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'исходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'happen / occur', paired with 'произойти'.

examples.text: Что происходит? Я не пойму.
examples.trans: What is going on? I don't understand.

examples.text: Что здесь происходит?
examples.trans: What is happening here?

examples.text: Мы не знаем, что с нашей дочерью происходит!
examples.trans: We don't know what is happening with our daughter!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.text: Да я просто заранее говорить не хотел.
examples.trans: I simply did not want to say anything in advance.

examples.text: Я хотел быть похожим на вас, а сейчас понял, что лучше Воронеж, чем с вами на одной кухне!
examples.trans: I wanted to be like you, and now I understood that Voronezh is better than being in the same kitchen with you!

examples.text: Я хочу кофе.
examples.trans: I want coffee.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ура, предлагаю нам отметить это!
examples.trans: Hooray, I propose we celebrate this!

examples.text: Уже нет, у тебя выходной сегодня с этой минуты.
examples.trans: Not anymore, you have a day off today starting this minute.

examples.text: Очень хорошо, что ты это помнишь.
examples.trans: It is very good that you remember that.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'брый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good').

examples.text: Доброе утро, ты разве не уволился?
examples.trans: Good morning, did you not quit?

examples.text: Добрый вечер!
examples.trans: Good evening!

examples.text: Она очень добрая.
examples.trans: She is very kind.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'really, can it be', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы же с тобой в кино ходили три раза.
examples.trans: After all, you and I went to the movies three times.

examples.text: Ну, раз целовались, значит, мы встречаемся.
examples.trans: Well, since we kissed, that means we are dating.

examples.text: А он мне заявил, что развлекаться надо вечером.
examples.trans: And he declared to me that one must have fun in the evening.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'волиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'quit / resigned'.

examples.text: Скажите, вы хотите меня уволить?
examples.trans: Tell me, do you want to fire me?

examples.text: Слушай, может, мне и правда уволиться?
examples.trans: Listen, maybe I really should quit?

examples.text: Макс, может, тебе правда надо уволиться?
examples.trans: Max, maybe you really should quit?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Сегодня не могу.
examples.trans: I can't today.

examples.text: Этого не может быть.
examples.trans: That can't be.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to accept, hire', paired with 'принимать'.

examples.text: Всё, договорились, твоё условие принято.
examples.trans: That is it, we agreed, your condition is accepted.

examples.text: Да, Лена, я уже хорошее лекарство принял.
examples.trans: Yes, Lena, I already took some good medicine.

examples.text: Нет, мы можем принять их или пытаться остаться в прошлом.
examples.trans: No, we can accept them or try to stay in the past.

meanings.en: to try, to attempt, to make an effort
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'try', paired with 'попытаться'.

examples.text: Нет, мы можем принять их или пытаться остаться в прошлом.
examples.trans: No, we can accept them or try to stay in the past.

examples.text: Я пыталась!
examples.trans: I tried!

examples.text: Он пытался объяснить ситуацию.
examples.trans: He tried to explain the situation.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to remain, to be left', paired with 'оставаться'.

examples.text: Нет, мы можем принять их или пытаться остаться в прошлом.
examples.trans: No, we can accept them or try to stay in the past.

examples.text: Ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: There's nothing left.

examples.text: Я останусь дома.
examples.trans: I'll stay at home.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'шлый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('last, past').

examples.text: Ты здесь как немой укор из прошлого.
examples.trans: You are here like a silent reproach from the past.

examples.text: Вика уже в прошлом, а работа нормальная.
examples.trans: Vika is already in the past, and the job is normal.

examples.text: Нет, мы можем принять их или пытаться остаться в прошлом.
examples.trans: No, we can accept them or try to stay in the past.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hello', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Здравствуйте, уважаемый Дмитрий Владимирович.
examples.trans: Hello, respected Dmitry Vladimirovich.

examples.text: Лёва, здравствуй, можно мне снова у тебя пожить?
examples.trans: Lyova, hello, may I stay at your place again?

examples.text: Здравствуй, Самсон.
examples.trans: Hello, Samson.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Витя, можешь идти куда хочешь.
examples.trans: Vitya, you can go wherever you want.

examples.text: Если, конечно, футбол тебе дороже, чем я.
examples.trans: If, of course, football is dearer to you than I am.

examples.text: Хорошо, милая, как скажешь, так и будет.
examples.trans: Alright, darling, as you say, so it will be.

meanings.en: to live for some time, to stay
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'stay / live for a while', paired with 'жить'.

examples.text: Ребята, скажите, как поживает ваш орёл?
examples.trans: Guys, tell us, how is your Eagle doing?

examples.text: Лёва, здравствуй, можно мне снова у тебя пожить?
examples.trans: Lyova, hello, may I stay at your place again?

examples.text: Лёва, можно у тебя пожить?
examples.trans: Lyova, may I stay at your place?
